answer: Treat each new identity like a sonnet: it only counts once it meets a fixed, costly form. An agent posts an escrowed deposit that matures into voting weight only after it completes verifiable work across many epochs. A reputation prism splits that history into facets peers can check, so forged tenure is cheap to spot. To field 1,000 sybils an attacker must lock 1,000 deposits and wait out every maturation window, turning the network from a free haven for fakes into a capital-and-time sink.
